meta.phase-name: Authored Room Entry Events And Dialogue Flow

phase-plan.purpose: Move the authored interaction pillar onto the real runtime by using the content packs for room-entry cutscenes, tightening room-feature action presentation in the shell, and flattening dialogue/cutscene flow into the live navigation loop.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: authored cutscene trigger definitions, room-entry cutscene support, shell room-action alignment, room-level narrative surfacing, and planning/docs sync. Out of scope for this slice: full NPC/entity authored binding overhaul and mana-resource convergence.

file.description: Canonical authored cutscene definitions should carry text and trigger rules instead of leaving the runtime on hardcoded defaults.
Generated runtime cutscene pack should mirror the richer authored trigger definitions.
The cutscene pack schema should define text and trigger fields for authored room-entry beats.
Cutscene runtime should read authored pack definitions and support room-entry trigger kinds.
The main runtime loop should pass room context into cutscene triggering and record authored room-entry beats in the event log.
The shell should surface room narrative/cutscene context and show the correct room-feature actions.
Shared room narrative helpers should expose recent room-level narrative state to the shell.
Document that authored cutscene logic now comes from the content pack and note the remaining interaction gaps.

task.description: Replace hardcoded default-cutscene definitions with content-pack-driven trigger definitions.
Add authored room-entry cutscene trigger kinds and record those beats through the main runtime event flow.
Flatten shell interaction flow by surfacing room narrative context and fixing room-feature action presentation.
Push farther into room-entry authored events and stronger NPC/entity bindings beyond the initial cutscene-driven slice.

decision.summary: Cutscene trigger logic belongs in the authored cutscene pack, not in hardcoded runtime defaults.
decision.impact: The editor/content pipeline now owns room-entry and milestone beats, and future consumers can use the same authored trigger payload without duplicating logic.

decision.summary: Room-entry narrative should surface through the existing navigation shell and event log rather than a separate debug feed.
decision.impact: Cutscenes and dialogue cues stay inside the same room loop the player is already using, which keeps the KAPLAY shell coherent while authored interaction depth grows.
